answer: Because the glacier index resolves every citation against the sparrow checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the mesa audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 230 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 230 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 4492 identities would post 1763 proofs and burn roughly 44 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
